numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Calling np.resize with an unsigned integer new_shape (np.uint32(1)) emits RuntimeWarning 'overflow encountered in scalar negative' at the repeats = -(-new_size // a.size) line and then raises SystemError: <built-in function concatenate> returned NULL without setting an exception; the unsigned negation underflows and creates a large positive repeats value. With np.uint64(1) the call raises OverflowError: cannot fit 'numpy.uint64' into an index-sized integer.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: np.resize(np.array([[23, 95], [66, 37]]), np.uint32(1)) should return the same result as with np.int32(1), i.e. print res = [23]; no warning, no SystemError, and no OverflowError for np.uint64(1).
trigger_conditions: new_shape/new_size passed as an unsigned integer type such as np.uint32 or np.uint64
array a is non-empty (a.size nonzero) so the ceiling-division repeats path is reached

oracle_clues: Reproducer in issue #29225 prints res = [23] for np.int32(1) as the reference behaviour
Fix replaces repeats = -(-new_size // a.size) with repeats = (new_size + a.size - 1) // a.size (ceiling division without negating new_size)
Fix is in numpy/_core/fromnumeric.py lines 1607-1614, backported in PR #29233 for issue #29225

numerical_characteristics.dtype: uint32 and uint64 (unsigned size arguments to np.resize; the issue also shows np.int32 and np.int64 as the working signed counterparts)
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Negating an unsigned size underflows and produces a large positive repeats value; the passages do not give the exact numeric value.
category_specific_evidence: Commit message: the negation of an unsigned int underflows and creates a large positive repeats, which leads to allocation failures and/or swapping.
Issue #29225 reproducer: np.resize(..., np.uint32(1)) raises SystemError from concatenate.
Issue #29225 reproducer: np.resize(..., np.uint64(1)) raises OverflowError: cannot fit 'numpy.uint64' into an index-sized integer.
Traceback shows RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in scalar negative at repeats = -(-new_size // a.size).
Violated formula: ceiling division ceil(new_size / a.size) computed as -(-new_size // a.size) breaks when new_size is unsigned; the fix uses (new_size + a.size - 1) // a.size.
Regression test test_unsigned_resize asserts np.resize(arr, np.int32(1)) equals np.resize(arr, np.uint32(1)) and the int64/uint64 pair for arr = [[23, 95], [66, 37]].
reproduction_risks: The exact overflowed repeats value and the failing allocation size are not stated in the passages.
Platform and NumPy version specifics beyond 'NumPy 2.x (tested on v2.3.0 and v2.2.5)' are not given.
Failure symptoms (SystemError versus OverflowError) depend on the unsigned width used, as shown by the uint32 and uint64 cases.
